newsitem.title: POLAND: Tenneco, GM bid for Polish shock absorber plant.
newsitem.headline: Tenneco, GM bid for Polish shock absorber plant.

text.p: Polish National Investment Fund No.6 "Magna Polonia" is in talks with U.S. Tenneco and a General Motors unit Delphi on selling its stake in a shock absorber plant, the fund's president said on Monday.
The Magna Polonia fund has 33 percent of the Krosnienskie Fabryki Amortyzatorow plant, one of the 514 companies taking part in Poland's mass privatisation programme.
The scheme's 14 other National Investment Funds have 27 percent, employees 15 percent and the state treasury 25 percent of the company.

"We have two excellent investors bidding to buy shares of the company. We will talk about the sale with other investment funds today and meet representatives of the state treasury next week," fund president Krzysztof Bialowolski told Reuters.
PAP news agency quoted an unnamed representative of the Polish Tenneco unit as saying the U.S. firm was ready to invest $30 million in the plant if it won the tender.
